S48.01.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.01.note: The button only appears when the field is empty and voice is allowed (canUseVoice); the binding to this chat was not traced beyond the code lines in the plan.
steps: Sign in and open an existing chat from the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty and look at the right end of the composer.
Click the button labelled "Start voice mode".
Check that the voice view opens in this chat and that the chat's earlier messages are still there.
S48.01.where: Open an existing chat > bottom composer, with the text field empty > "Start voice mode" button at the right end of the composer

S48.02.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.02.note: The same button is shown on the new-chat composer (ChatComposerNew), but the code I opened did not show a separate new-chat-creation step for voice.
steps: Sign in and click New chat in the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty and find the "Start voice mode" button at the right end of the composer.
Click it and check that voice starts in a new chat.
S48.02.where: New chat > bottom composer, with the text field empty > "Start voice mode" button

S48.03.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.03.note: I did not confirm from the code whether the voice view sits over the chat or replaces it; the transcript placement is only cited as line references.
steps: Open a chat and click "Start voice mode" with the text field empty.
Speak one turn, then type one message in the "Type a message to send as a normal turn" field.
Look at the chat's message list and check that spoken and typed turns appear in the same list.
S48.03.where: Open a chat > "Start voice mode" button in the composer > voice view

S48.04.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.04.note: The full-screen layout is in VoiceModeSurface.tsx, but I did not confirm the exact size from the code.
steps: Click "Start voice mode" from the composer of any chat.
Check whether the voice view fills the window, with the orb in the centre.
Check whether the transcript is hidden or shown in a smaller area.
S48.04.where: Open a chat > "Start voice mode" button in the composer > voice view fills the window

S48.05.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.05.note: The listening state is drawn by VoiceOrb (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/VoiceOrb.tsx) and the state machine (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice/voice-session-machine.ts), but I did not find a visible word for the listening state, so I could not give the exact path to it.

S48.06.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.06.note: The speaking state is drawn by VoiceOrb and live-voice-session.ts, but I did not find its visible words; the "Tap to hear the assistant" text is a different state (audio blocked).

S48.07.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.07.note: The visible text is from the LABEL constant; the exact moment it shows was not traced.
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Ask for something that needs a tool, such as a search.
While the reply is still working, look for the status text "Working on your request".
Compare it with the orb's thinking or working look.
S48.07.where: Start voice mode > ask a question that needs a tool or a long answer > the status line while the reply is working

S48.08.note: The visual follows audio level in VoiceOrb.tsx; it has no control of its own.
steps: Start voice mode and speak.
Watch the orb while you talk and while the reply plays.
Check that the orb's shape changes with the loudness of the sound.
S48.08.where: Inside the voice view, the orb in the middle of the screen

S48.09.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the microphone button in the bottom bar; its label is "Turn off microphone".
Check that the button changes to "Turn on microphone" and the call stays open.
Click again and check the microphone is back on without the call ending.
S48.09.where: Start voice mode > bottom bar of the voice view > microphone button labelled "Turn off microphone"

S48.10.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.10.note: The settling of usage is not visible on screen; I did not check it.
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the button labelled "End voice session" in the bottom bar.
Check that the voice view closes and the call stops.
Check the chat still shows the conversation.
S48.10.where: Start voice mode > bottom bar of the voice view > "End voice session" button

S48.11.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.11.note: The pause text says the call is closed, which may differ from the Expected line that says mic and assistant pause without ending.
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the "Open this chat panel" button in the voice bottom bar.
In the menu labelled "In this chat", click "Pause call".
Check the screen shows "Paused." text with a "Resume" button, then click "Resume" and check the call continues.
S48.11.where: Start voice mode > "Open this chat panel" button > "Pause call" item

S48.13.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.13.note: I searched apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice, the voice hook and packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice for hands-free and found no visible control or label for it.

S48.14.needs: a microphone and an external voice service
S48.14.note: Barge-in is a threshold rule (BARGE_IN_LEVEL_THRESHOLD) in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice/voice-session-machine.ts and has no control; I did not confirm it runs in the browser.
steps: Start voice mode and ask a question with a long answer.
While the assistant is speaking, speak loudly for a moment.
Check that the spoken reply stops and the app starts listening to you.
S48.14.where: Inside a voice reply, while the assistant is speaking

S48.15.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the "Voice settings" link at the top of the voice view.
In the dialog titled "Voice settings", use the arrows in the "Voice" section to change the voice.
Start a reply and check that the chosen voice is the one speaking.
S48.15.where: Start voice mode > "Voice settings" button at the top of the voice view > "Voice" carousel

S48.16.needs: a signed-in account with voice access
S48.16.note: Partly unfinished: the ledger says the sample manifest is empty so the button stays hidden until the owner generates the samples; the code does show the "Play sample" text when a sample is present.
steps: Open "Voice settings" from the top of the voice view.
Look at the voice carousel for a "Play sample" button.
Click "Play sample" and check that a short sample plays in that voice.
S48.16.where: Start voice mode > "Voice settings" > voice carousel > "Play sample" button

S48.17.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.17.note: Whether the choice reaches speech recognition was not confirmed from the code.
steps: Open "Voice settings" from the top of the voice view.
Find the "Language" section and pick a different language.
Start a new turn in voice and check the spoken language matches the choice.

S48.19.needs: a signed-in account with voice access, a microphone, and a second speaker or headphones
S48.19.note: The picker only appears where the browser supports changing the output device (setSinkId); not checked in the Electron window.
steps: Open "Voice settings" from the top of the voice view.
Find the "Audio output" control and open it.
Check the menu titled "Audio output device" lists "System default" and the other speakers.
Pick a speaker and check the next reply plays through it.
S48.19.where: Start voice mode > "Voice settings" > "Audio output" menu

S48.21.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click "Open this chat panel" and then "Captions".
Check a region labelled "Voice captions" appears.
Speak and let the assistant reply, then check both speakers' lines appear.
S48.21.where: Start voice mode > "Open this chat panel" button > "Captions" item

S48.22.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.22.note: The transcript code is cited at WebChatPage.tsx lines only; I did not find a visible label for the transcript itself.
steps: Start voice mode from a chat and have a short spoken exchange.
End the call with "End voice session".
Read the same chat's message list.
Check the spoken turns appear as a transcript kept with the chat.
S48.22.where: Start voice mode > speak a few turns > end the call > open the same chat and read the message list

S48.26.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.26.note: The control that opens the Activity panel was not traced; I only read the panel's labels.
steps: Start voice mode and ask for something that uses a tool.
Open the activity view during the turn (the "Activity" panel).
Check the tool steps and results are listed, and that the panel closes with "Close the activity panel".
S48.26.where: Start voice mode > "Activity" panel during a voice turn that uses a tool

S48.27.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
S48.27.note: The deny button's visible words were not found in the card file I searched.
steps: Start voice mode and ask for an action that needs approval.
When the approval card appears in the voice view, read its summary.
Click the approve button labelled "Approve" with the action name.
Check the reply continues without leaving the voice view.
S48.27.where: Start voice mode > ask for an action that needs approval > approval card in the voice view > "Approve" button

S48.28.needs: a signed-in account with voice access, a microphone, and a voice turn that creates a file
S48.28.note: The desktop window routing that decides where the file opens is in apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts; not traced in detail.
steps: Start voice mode and ask the assistant to create a document.
When the file appears in the voice view, click its "Open" button (its label includes the file name).
Check the document opens.
S48.28.where: Start voice mode > ask for a document > the file card in the voice view > "Open" button

S48.36.needs: a signed-in account with voice access, a microphone, and the ability to drop the network
S48.36.note: The message shown when reconnecting fails was not found in the label list.
steps: Start voice mode and speak once.
Turn Wi-Fi off for a few seconds, then back on.
Look for the "Reconnecting, attempt" notice with the count of attempts.
Check that the call reconnects or shows that it could not.
S48.36.where: Start voice mode > the connection drops (for example, turn off Wi-Fi for a moment) > "Reconnecting, attempt" notice

S48.37.needs: an account whose voice usage is used up (a Free account)
S48.37.note: The notice text itself was not found in the label list; only the Upgrade label and the data-testid voice-usage-limit were found.
steps: Start voice mode on an account whose voice usage is used up.
Look for the usage-limit notice in the voice view.
Click "Upgrade" and check the upgrade page opens.
S48.37.where: Start voice mode > when voice usage runs out > usage notice with "Upgrade" button

labels.text: Type a message to send as a normal turn

S48.38.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
steps: Start voice mode and have a spoken turn.
Click "Continue in text" in the voice view.
Type a message in the "Type a message to send as a normal turn" field and send it.
Check the reply continues in the same chat's text conversation.
S48.38.where: Start voice mode > "Continue in text" button in the voice view

S48.39.needs: a Free account or a paid account, a microphone, an existing chat with earlier messages
S48.39.note: The code loads earlier turns on the server (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts, loadLiveVoiceContext) and passes the current chat id, but there is no separate Resume button or history list for voice; the tester can only see the effect by asking about earlier content. Whether the voice view is bound to the same chat was confirmed from ChatComposerNew, not from a running session.
steps: Sign in and open an existing chat that already has earlier messages, from the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty. The round button at the right end of the message box shows Start voice mode (it is replaced by Send once you type).
Click Start voice mode and speak. The voice view opens in the same chat.
Ask about something said earlier in the chat by text. Compare: the reply should use the earlier turns, and the spoken turns should be added to the same chat, not a new one.
S48.39.where: Open an existing chat from the sidebar > leave the message box empty > Start voice mode

S48.40.needs: a paid or Free account that can use Remote Control, a paired Desktop computer that accepts tasks, a microphone
S48.40.note: Steering here is speech-to-text dictation into the task box (useDictation), not a live voice conversation, and the strip's send button label was not checked. The same dictation strip also appears in the Code composer (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeComposer.tsx). Whether the sidebar item is visible depends on the Remote Control feature flag (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts).
steps: Sign in on the web app and pair a Desktop computer first (Desktop: Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control, Pair a phone, Copy link for a browser; then paste it under Your computer).
Open Code in the sidebar, then click Your computer in the rail.
Under the heading Connected to ..., click inside the Task box, then click the microphone button with the label Start voice input.
Speak the task, then use the controls on the dictation strip to stop or send. Compare: the spoken words should appear as the task you send to the computer, and no reply is spoken back.
S48.40.where: Code > Your computer > Connected to ... > Task box > Start voice input

S48.41.needs: a microphone, a voice task that starts a running action
S48.41.note: Found only half of the item. During a voice call, a Stop the task button appears in the status line while an action runs (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx, line 596 cancelBackendWork, hint Stops the running action and keeps the call open.). No separate control to stop only the spoken reply was found in VoiceModeSurface.tsx, VoiceComposer, use-voice-session.ts or live-voice-session.ts. Searched for Stop, interrupt, cancel and response.cancel in those files.
